div.head: Norðleoda 7
div.ab: And gif Wilisman geþeo, þæt he hæbbe hiwisc landes ⁊ mæge cyninges gafol forðbringan, þonne bið his wergild CXX scill'.
⁊ gif Wilisc man geþeo, þæt he hæbbe hywisc landes ⁊ mage cynges gafel forðbringan, þonne byð his wergyld CCXX scill'.
And Wealiscmonnes wergild, gif he beo to ðam gewelegod, þæt he hyred⁊ eht age ⁊ ðam cyng gafol gyldan mæg, hit biþ ðon CCXX scill.
Et si Waliscus promoueatur, ut habeat familiam et terram et possit gablum regis reddere, tunc est wera eius CCXX sol.
And gif Wilise man geþeo þæt he hæbbe hywisc landes and mage cynges gafel forðbringan, þonne byð his wergild CCXX scillinga.
Und wenn ein Wälscher [so] emporkommt, dass er 1 Hid Landes besitzt und Steuer [direct] an den König aufzubringen vermag, dann ist sein Wergeld 120 Schill. (220 hlq).
And if a Welshman prospers [so] that he holds 1 hide of land and can pay tax [directly] to the king, then his wergild is 120 shillings (220, hlq).
And if a Welshman prospers, that he has a hide of land and may produce the king's tribute, then his wergild is 120 shillings.
And if a Welshman prospers so that he possesses a hide of land and can pay the king's tribute, then his wergild shall be two hundred and twenty shillings.

div.note: D reads CXX; H's CCXX is a corruption in hlq (likewise below Mirce 3). Liebermann notes that clauses 7–12 are, according to Schmid, a later extension, probably southern-English influenced. Ld: ‘a Welshman's wergild, if he has become so rich that he has a household and property and can pay the king tax: it is 220 shillings’. Liebermann compares Ine 32.; AY: corrected against Rabin p. 12 / 13, October 2026 (was “ccxx: cxx”, now “CCXX: CXX”)

Hier beginnt ein inhaltlich und stilistisch verschiedenes Stück B; s. o. Einl. 1.—Ines Gesetzbuch kann nach Northumbrien nicht vor Eadwards I. dortigen Erfolgen gedrungen sein.—Um das Auftreten des Wallisers—vielleicht eine blosse Kompilatorlaune des Sammlers um 1050—zu erklären, denkt Schmid S. lxvi hier an Westmercien, wo die Thrymsen-Rechnung aber nicht belegt ist. Doch gab es auch im westlichen Northumbrien Walliser

Here begins a piece B different in content and style; see above Introduction 1. — Ine’s code cannot have reached Northumbria before Eadward I’s successes there. — To explain the appearance of the Welshman — perhaps a mere compiler’s whim of the collector of c. 1050 — Schmid p. lxvi thinks here of West Mercia, where, however, reckoning in thrymsas is not attested. But there were Welshmen in western Northumbria too
eines Wälschen Wergeld, wenn er zu dém [Grade] reich geworden ist, dass er Haushalt und Vermögen besitzt und dem K. S. zu zahlen v.: es ist d. 220 S. Ld; vgl. 9
a Welshman’s wergild, if he has become rich to such [a degree] that he possesses household and property and is able to pay the king’s tax: it is then 220 shill. Ld; cf. 9
Dieselbe Wendung, auch 7, 1. 9. 10. 11. 12, hängt stilistisch mit Geþyncðo zusammen.—Systematisch merzt lq das Verb geþeon aus; s. S. 256 n. 4; dieselbe Ersetzung wie hier auch u. 9
The same phrase, also in 7, 1. 9. 10. 11. 12, is stylistically connected with Geþyncðo. — lq systematically eliminates the verb geþeon; see p. 256 n. 4; the same substitution as here also below 9
